title: The Only Deity and the Blessed Night

paragraphs.text: Allah alone is the deity in the heaven and the only deity on the earth, and He is the Wise, the Knowing. Blessed is He who owns the heavens and the earth and everything between them; He alone has knowledge of when the Hour will come, and to Him all will be returned. The ones people call upon besides Him have no power to intercede, except those who bear witness to the truth with knowledge. If the disbelievers are asked who created them, they will surely answer, "Allah," so how can they be so deluded and turned away from worshipping Him? Allah takes note of the Prophet's words when he complained, "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe." He is told to turn away from them and say, "Peace," because they will soon know the truth.

A new surah opens with Ha, Meem, and an oath by the clear Book. Allah sent this Book down during a blessed night, because He has always intended to warn mankind. On that night every precise matter is set apart, as a command from Allah. He was going to send a messenger as a mercy from the Lord, the Hearing, the Knowing. He is Lord of the heavens, the earth and all that lies between them, if only people would be certain of it. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death, and He is their Lord and the Lord of their earliest forefathers.

Yet the disbelievers remain in doubt, amusing themselves and not taking the message seriously. So the Prophet is told to watch and wait for a coming Day, when the sky will bring forth a smoke that everyone can see. It will spread over the people and cover them, and it will be a painful torment for them.
